authority: This file is authoritative for Onyx animation. Any older prototype field resembling hunger, energy, attention, affection, comfort, or another draining motive is superseded and must not be implemented.

needs_free.rule: Hungry and sleepy are names for readable expressions and context-triggered animation families only. They do not store, drain, refill, or punish.

anatomy.ordinary_animation: Natural four-legged cat anatomy at all times.
anatomy.professor_exception: Professor Onyx is the only human-like/upright family. He remains cat-sized, unclothed, and may hold only a clipboard.
anatomy.reference_translation: Pose images are attitude and silhouette references. Any ordinary pose that appears too anthropomorphic must be translated into a natural quadruped or natural seated-cat performance in the final rig.

presentation.geometry: Onyx, room, furniture, collision, lighting, and animation are technically three-dimensional.
presentation.camera: Limited fixed or softly transitioning camera presets make the scene read as slightly two-dimensional.
presentation.style: Controlled perspective, silhouette staging, held poses, limited animation, line/shape readability, and restrained parallax create the 2.5D result.

pose_references.name: Front View
pose_references.description: Neutral proportion and facial-symmetry reference. Use for rig checks, eye line, chest width, paw spacing, and front-facing dialogue framing.

pose_references.name: Front Three-Quarter Left
pose_references.description: Primary left-facing conversation and Home View reference. Preserve the broad chest, long torso, large paws, and readable green-gold eyes.

pose_references.name: Left Profile
pose_references.description: Side silhouette reference for body length, shoulder height, primordial-pouch motion, head carriage, and long thin tail.

pose_references.name: Rear Three-Quarter Left
pose_references.description: Rear-left staging reference for hind-leg placement, tail follow-through, turn cycles, and walking away without losing Onyx’s silhouette.

pose_references.name: Rear View
pose_references.description: Rear proportion and gait reference. Keeps the body broad and heavy without turning him into a fluffy or round generic cat.

pose_references.name: Rear Three-Quarter Right
pose_references.description: Mirrored rear staging reference for exits, furniture approaches, tail-safe clearances, and rightward turns.

pose_references.name: Right Profile
pose_references.description: Right-side silhouette reference for walk, pause, stretch, approach, and object-use cycles.

pose_references.name: Front Three-Quarter Right
pose_references.description: Primary right-facing conversation and Home View reference, paired with pose 02 for the limited camera set.

pose_references.name: Front Hero Pose
pose_references.description: Confident neutral presentation for arrival, purchase reaction, wardrobe preview, profile selection, and celebratory holds.

pose_references.name: High-Angle View
pose_references.description: Elevated 2.5D reference for Decor and limited inspection presets. This is a camera/framing guide, not permission for unrestricted orbit.

pose_references.name: Hungry Expression — Non-Need
pose_references.description: A tongue-out, food-aware reaction used only when food, treats, a bowl, a package sound, or food dialogue is already present. It never represents a hunger meter, decay, neglect, or required feeding.

pose_references.name: Professor Onyx
pose_references.description: The only human-like pose family: still cat-sized, briefly upright in a talking-animal posture, unclothed, and holding only a clipboard. All other poses remain natural four-legged cat animation.

pose_references.name: Thinking
pose_references.description: A natural seated-cat pause with head tilt, eye tracking, ear adjustment, and a restrained forepaw gesture. The reference supplies attitude; the final rig must not become bipedal.

pose_references.name: Caring
pose_references.description: A gentle approach, soft eyes, low head, slow blink, and optional natural forepaw reach. Used for reassurance and check-ins without turning Onyx into a generic helper mascot.

pose_references.name: Thoughtful
pose_references.description: A longer reflective hold with breathing, ear listening, small head movement, and delayed eye focus. Distinct from Thinking by its slower, quieter timing.

pose_references.name: Listening
pose_references.description: Attentive ear orientation, eye contact, head tilt, still body, and occasional slow blink. Onyx stops irrelevant activity and visibly follows the user’s actual words.

pose_references.name: Snuggly
pose_references.description: A curled, side-lying, leaning, or close-settling family with weight compression, tail wrap, kneading options, and purr vibration. It is always optional and user-invited.

pose_references.name: Sleepy Expression — Non-Need
pose_references.description: Heavy eyelids, yawn, slow blink, reduced head lift, and voluntary settling. It is an expressive choice or scene response, never an energy meter or obligation to make him sleep.

pose_references.name: Judgmental
pose_references.description: Narrowed eyes, stillness, angled ears, delayed blink, tiny head turn, and restrained tail-tip punctuation for Onyx’s dry comedic reactions.

pose_references.name: Purring
pose_references.description: Eyes softened or closed, relaxed upright tail or curled tail, subtle chest/throat vibration, breathing loop, and optional kneading. Purring may continue during quiet dialogue or snuggling.

Core locomotion and posture.name: Idle / breathing
Core locomotion and posture.description: Low-amplitude chest, shoulder, whisker, ear, eye, and tail motion. Uses held poses and short loops rather than constant full-body movement.

Core locomotion and posture.name: Walk
Core locomotion and posture.description: Heavy but agile quadruped gait with shoulder roll, paw spread, pouch follow-through, and tail counterbalance.

Core locomotion and posture.name: Leash walk
Core locomotion and posture.description: Natural four-legged walk with harness/leash contact, pace matching, pause, look-back, and route-aware turns.

Core locomotion and posture.name: Sit, stay, come
Core locomotion and posture.description: Readable trained responses with anticipatory ear/head motion and no obedience meter.

Core locomotion and posture.name: Climb and jump
Core locomotion and posture.description: Approach, crouch, launch, landing compression, large-paw contact, balance recovery, and safe furniture anchors.

Core locomotion and posture.name: Loaf
Core locomotion and posture.description: Forepaws tucked, chest settled, tail placed safely, blinking and ear/tail micro-movement.

Core locomotion and posture.name: Stretch
Core locomotion and posture.description: Full 38–44-inch body allowance, shoulder extension, paw spread, back arch, pouch movement, and long-tail follow-through.

Rest and affection.name: Sleep and wake
Rest and affection.description: Voluntary sleep loops plus wake-by-petting, gentle user interaction, treat-bag sound, or opened food context. No sleep debt or energy value exists.

Rest and affection.name: Snuggle
Rest and affection.description: Lean, curl, settle, compress soft surfaces, purr, knead, and slow blink while preserving natural cat anatomy.

Rest and affection.name: Knead
Rest and affection.description: Alternating front paws, shoulder shift, claw-safe surface contact, purr option, and soft-object deformation.

Rest and affection.name: Slow blink
Rest and affection.description: A short facial/eyelid layer that can overlay listening, caring, snuggling, sitting, or loafing.

Rest and affection.name: Pet response
Rest and affection.description: Head push, cheek rub, shoulder lean, back arch, tail response, or politely moving away according to context.

Voice, expression, and support.name: Meow and yowl
Voice, expression, and support.description: Mouth, throat, whisker, ear, and head motion synchronized to the selected audio; no attention meter drives vocalization.

Voice, expression, and support.name: Purr
Voice, expression, and support.description: Subtle body vibration, breath rhythm, relaxed face, and optional kneading or tail posture.

Voice, expression, and support.name: Thinking / thoughtful
Voice, expression, and support.description: Two timing families: active problem-solving versus quiet reflection.

Voice, expression, and support.name: Listening / caring
Voice, expression, and support.description: Context-aware stillness, eye/ear focus, slow approach, and grounded reactions to serious conversation.

Voice, expression, and support.name: Judgmental / refusal
Voice, expression, and support.description: Dry pause, narrowed eyes, tail-tip punctuation, turn-away, reluctant acceptance, or eventual compliance where appropriate.

Voice, expression, and support.name: Service alert
Voice, expression, and support.description: Specific trained alert posture, route, contact behavior, and follow-up hold; never a random reward animation.

Voice, expression, and support.name: Professor
Voice, expression, and support.description: Only cat-sized upright talking-animal family; unclothed and clipboard-only.

Object and room interaction.name: Eat and drink
Object and room interaction.description: Optional bowl scenes with sniff, taste, eat/drink, pause, approval, rejection, and walk-away variants. These are not need fulfillment.

Object and room interaction.name: Groom and scratch
Object and room interaction.description: Natural self-grooming, scratching-post contacts, stretch, claw placement, and fur/pouch secondary motion.

Object and room interaction.name: Play and investigate
Object and room interaction.description: User-engaged swat, chase, bite, carry, inspect, sniff, paw, and ignore variants; play is not a required need.

Object and room interaction.name: Furniture entry and exit
Object and room interaction.description: Approach anchors, step-up, circle, settle, curl/stretch, rise, jump-down, and tail-safe clearance.

Object and room interaction.name: Purchase and layout reactions
Object and room interaction.description: Inspect new item, circle it, use it, approve, judge, refuse, reluctantly accept, or comment through a held readable pose.

Object and room interaction.name: Clothing preview
Object and room interaction.description: Stand, sit, turn, stretch, walk, and react while checking shoulders, chest, belly, legs, paws, and tail for clipping.

Object and room interaction.name: Tablet bird watching
Object and room interaction.description: Onyx faces away, blocks the screen, watches for exactly the selected audio duration, and returns naturally when it ends.
